main_text.p: ὀρχεῖσθαι ὑπὲρ τὴν κόρδακα.] Quantum fit ponderis in voce ὑφῶν, licet intelligere ex eo quod Demosthenes in secunda Olynthiaca pro argumento vitæ penitus dissolutæ sociorum Philippi, ait cos ubi largiùs poti fuerint, solitos cordacem saltare. Multo enim turpius si quis siccus cordacem saltet, quàm si madidus. Est autem cordax lasciuæ & comicæ saltationis genus: ideo ait ἐν κωμικῷ χορῷ. Aristophanes verò in Nebulis gloriatur in suis comœdiis huic saltationi nullum esse locum. Puto autem ad restim solitum cordacem saltari: nam Aristophanes pro κορδακίζειν dixit κόρδακα ἐλκυστήν. Iulianus & alij ἐλκεῖν κόρδακα.
καὶ προσωπεῖον ἔχων ἐν κωμικῷ χορῷ.] Falsi suspe-

page.notes: Greek words in the first paragraphs are only partly legible at this scan resolution; the readings marked [?] are doubtful. The passage from Polybius (τυχὸν ... ἀτρυφῆ) is illegible in its middle and is marked as such. Catchword: none visible. The word "Falsi" at the end is printed as "Falfi" (long s); it is given here as a plain s. The line "Falfi fufpe-" is the last full line and is a hyphenated break, so it stays as printed.
